question: What will India's June–September 2026 southwest monsoon seasonal rainfall be, as a percentage of the Long Period Average, per IMD?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: end-of-season all-India departures for years where the cumulative reading around 20 Sep was already fixed — with ~92% of the season elapsed and only ~55.6 mm of seasonal normal left, the final figure is arithmetically pinned near the current reading. 693 mm banked to 18 Sep is 79.8% of LPA; a residual exactly at normal lands ~86.2, and the ratio drifts UP ~1 point from the 85 cumulative reading because that 85 is against a to-date normal, not the full LPA. Adjusting off that anchor: a deep depression crossing south Odisha-north AP ~23 Sep and tracking WNW over Chhattisgarh/Telangana/Vidarbha with widespread rain into Jharkhand/Bihar/WB is a concrete above-normal forcing for the exact residual window, while IMD's below-normal September outlook, NW withdrawal from 19 Sep, and a ~29% South Peninsula deficit pull the other way. Net roughly neutral-to-slightly-up on the mechanical anchor, so median 86.2 with most mass on integers 85-87. Upside escape (>92.5) needs ~2x normal rain over the last 11 days via a re-intensifying or second Bay system: priced at 1.5%. No downside escape declared — <79.5 is unreachable given the banked total. No human market exists on this contract, so no blend; primary IMD portal was unreachable this run, so the current cumulative rests on news reporting of IMD figures.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off IMD's FIRST officially published end-of-season all-India figure for 'The Country As A Whole', 1 Jun-30 Sep 2026, as a percentage of the 1971-2020 LPA of 868.6 mm — not off any in-season cumulative bulletin, not off Skymet, not off a later revision. A whole-percent departure, if that is the earliest form published, determines resolution. IMD has in past years published a one-decimal value (2023 season: 94.4%; 2024 season: reported both as 107.6% and rounded to 108%), so the published form may be integer or one-decimal.

EVENT WINDOW: 2026-06-01 -> 2026-09-30 per the resolution criteria (122 days). As of Now = 2026-09-21T06:20Z, 112.3 of 122 days = 92.0% elapsed. Residual window = 19-30 September.

ACCOUNTING FACTS (all from IMD figures as reported):
- 1 Jun-16 Sep 2026: actual 682.0 mm vs normal 801.5 mm, departure -15% (IMD extended-range press release, 17 Sep 2026).
- 1 Jun-18 Sep 2026: actual 693 mm, departure -15% (IMD via Indian Express, 19 Sep 2026).
- Monthly 2026: June 106.8 mm vs 165 mm normal (-35%); July 283.3 mm vs 280.5 mm normal (+1%, only surplus month); August 213.3 mm vs 254.9 mm normal, 7th lowest August since 2001 (IMD via News18, 19 Sep 2026).
- Implied: Sept 1-18 actual ~89.6 mm against a Sept 1-18 normal of ~112.6 mm; full-September normal ~168 mm; normal remaining for 19-30 Sep ~55.6 mm (~4.6 mm/day).
- Conversion: 8.7 mm of all-India rainfall = 1.0 percentage point of the 868.6 mm LPA. Mapping from residual rain R (19-30 Sep) to final percentage: R=20 -> 82.1; R=35 -> 83.8; R=45 -> 85.0; R=55.6 (exactly normal) -> 86.2; R=70 -> 87.8; R=85 -> 89.5; R=110 -> 92.4.
- Hard floor: 693 mm already banked = 79.8% of LPA regardless of what happens next.

WET-SIDE EVIDENCE:
- Low-pressure area over north Andaman Sea 19 Sep, forecast to become a depression 21 Sep, a deep depression 22 Sep, and cross the south Odisha-north Andhra Pradesh coast around 23 Sep morning (IMD via ThePrint / Indian Express, 19-20 Sep 2026).

Odisha put 20 districts on alert.
- July 2026 came in at +1%, showing the season is capable of normal months.

DRY-SIDE EVIDENCE:
- Southwest monsoon withdrawal began from parts of West Rajasthan on 19 Sep, 2 days after the 17 Sep climatological normal; IMD expected further withdrawal from Rajasthan, Punjab, Saurashtra and Kutch within 3-4 days (IMD, 19 Sep 2026).

- Regional departures 1 Jun-16 Sep: Central India -5%, Northwest -10%, East & NE -26%, South Peninsula -28% (-29% by 19 Sep) — the two most deficient regions are the ones with the largest late-September normals.
- Sept 1-18 ran roughly 20% below its own normal; IMD's monthly outlook for September was below normal, and the 17 Sep extended-range release forecast continued below-normal September rainfall.
- Attributed drivers: El Nino conditions emerging over the equatorial Pacific in June, unfavourable MJO phases, and fewer low-pressure systems during key periods (IMD).

BASE RATES, WITH THE CLASS EACH IS COMPUTED OVER:
- Over the residual-window class (all seasons since 2001, share of the 868.6 mm seasonal normal falling 19-30 Sep): ~6.4% of the LPA, i.e. the maximum arithmetic room left is small in both directions.
- Over the conditional class (seasons whose ~20 Sep cumulative was already deficient): the final percentage-of-LPA differs from the late-September cumulative reading by roughly +1 point when the residual is exactly normal, because the in-season percentage is computed against a to-date normal rather than the full LPA — the direction of this drift is upward, its size is bounded by the bullet above.
- Over the all-seasons class (unconditional, 1901-2025): deficient seasons (<90% of LPA) are the minority of years; nearest recent analogues by final value are 2015 at 86% (13th lowest on record) and 2014, also deficient; 2009 was 18% below normal; 2023 ended 94.4%; 2024 ended 108%.
- Over the class of El Nino-coincident seasons specifically: monsoon suppression is the modal outcome, which is the condition already realised in the observed data above rather than additional independent evidence.

PRIOR OFFICIAL FORECASTS (for context on what the season was expected to do, not on what it did): IMD first-stage 13 Apr 2026 = 92% of LPA +/-5%; IMD update 29 May 2026 = 90% of LPA with a stated 60% chance of a deficient season; Skymet ~85%; Reuters 24 Aug 2026 reported a course toward ~15% below LPA; Bloomberg 18 Sep 2026 framed the season as the driest since 2009 if the deficit holds.

RESOLUTION-TIMING NOTE: the season ends 30 Sep; scheduled resolution is 2026-10-02T00:00Z. ARITHMETIC IDENTITY (do this yourself): final % of LPA = (cumulative mm through the last reported date + rainfall over the remaining days) / 868.6 x 100. 1 percentage point of LPA = 8.686 mm of all-India rainfall.

OBSERVED 2026 DATA

- Regional departures as of mid-September (IMD 17 Sep): Central India -5%, Northwest India -10%, East & Northeast India -26%, South Peninsula -28% (South Peninsula quoted at -29% as of 19 Sep).

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD MORE RAIN IN THE REMAINING WINDOW
- Low-pressure area over north Andaman Sea/east-central Bay of Bengal; IMD (20 Sep 2026, via Business Today) expects intensification to a depression 21 Sep, deep depression 22 Sep, crossing the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast the morning of 23 Sep.

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD LESS RAIN IN THE REMAINING WINDOW
- Southwest monsoon withdrawal commenced from parts of west Rajasthan on 19 Sep 2026 (two days after the 17 Sep climatological normal date), withdrawal line through Ramgarh, Mohangarh, Phalodi, Khajuwala; IMD expects further withdrawal from Rajasthan, Punjab, Saurashtra and Kutch within 3-4 days (IMD via Indian Express/News18, 19 Sep).
- IMD attributes the deficit to El Nino conditions that emerged over the equatorial Pacific in June, an unfavourable MJO, fewer low-pressure systems, and long dry spells; El Nino was reported as still strengthening in September.
- IMD's September 2026 monthly outlook was for below-normal rainfall over most of the country.
- Bloomberg (18 Sep 2026) reported an expected final seasonal deficit in the 13-16% band even allowing for a Bay of Bengal system developing later in the month.
- Sep 1-18 2026 ran roughly 21% below its own normal, i.e. the September shortfall was running deeper than the season-to-date shortfall.

FORECAST HISTORY FOR 2026 (for context on how the season was anticipated)
- IMD first-stage forecast 13 Apr 2026: 92% of LPA, 35% chance of a deficient season.
- IMD updated forecast 29 May 2026: 90% of LPA +/- 4%, 60% chance of a deficient season, 84% probability of below-normal-or-less.
- Skymet: around 85% of LPA. Reuters (24 Aug 2026): season ending around 15% below LPA.

BASE RATES, EACH WITH THE CLASS IT IS COMPUTED OVER
- Over all monsoon seasons 1901-2025 (unconditional): the all-India seasonal total is ~100% of LPA by construction; IMD's 'Deficient' category (<90%) occurs in roughly one season in seven.
- Over El Nino monsoon seasons specifically: below-normal outcomes predominate; recent deficient analogues cited by IMD and press are 2009 (~18% below LPA), 2014 and 2015 (2015 ended at 86% of LPA, 13th lowest on record). 2024 by contrast ended at 108%.
- Over the persistence class (final % of LPA vs the value implied by carrying the ~18 Sep cumulative forward at exactly-normal rain for the residual days, 1971-2025): the residual window moves the season total by only a small number of points because it carries ~6% of LPA; the 2021 example above is near the wet edge of that move.
- Conditional decomposition that matters here: 693 mm already banked = 79.8 points of the final figure; every additional 8.686 mm of all-India rain over 19-30 Sep adds one point.

SERIES DISPERSION NOTE: the quantity whose spread governs the remaining uncertainty is all-India area-weighted rainfall over 19-30 Sep (normal ~54.9 mm). Across recent years this has ranged from strongly sub-normal in early-withdrawal seasons to well above normal when a Bay depression or cyclone tracked inland.
